dispatch: Two Arkansas ACIC families, each carrying one recorded failed obligation named ARTIFACTS from lane vf90 at base a09ef20d342929fb68141828508f38e65a5a8545, both recorded in BORDER_COHORT_REMEDIATION as EVERY_STROKE_IS_THE_FORMS_OWN_SOME_WITH_ITS_BACKGROUND_FILL_STRIPPED. Decide the stripped fills on the pixels, per widget; restore what masked printed art and leave alone what masked blank paper.

howTheSourceWasRendered.why: A removed-dark-pixel count taken against an ANNOTATION-FREE render of an AcroForm source is worthless. An AcroForm keeps much of what the court prints inside widget /AP /N appearance streams, so an annotation-free source render is missing exactly the ink whose absence from the delivered page the difference is meant to detect: both sides come up blank in the same places and the difference is zero by construction.
howTheSourceWasRendered.renderer: poppler pdftoppm 24.02.0, invoked as `pdftoppm -r 600 -gray -aa yes -f <page> -l <page> <pdf> <prefix>`. Poppler draws widget annotations and applies ISO 32000-1 12.5.5; no flag suppressing annotations was passed and none exists on this tool.
howTheSourceWasRendered.threshold: grey < 128 counts as a dark pixel, at 600 dpi, on 5100x6600 letter pages.
howTheSourceWasRendered.provedNotAssumed: The same command was run over the pinned ACIC order (b347754fd115adea52068fe5cd267f84021f8f435a7b86c02c3347dd86f9f555) and over a control copy of it with every page /Annots and the catalog /AcroForm removed. Page 1 renders 1,926,487 dark pixels normally and 1,922,979 with annotations removed. 9,622 dark pixels on that page are drawn by annotations ALONE and by nothing in page content, and the difference bounding box (x 881-1030, y 3984-4291 at 600 dpi) falls exactly on the two check-box /Rect values the source declares on that page. The render draws widget /AP /N ink, so a zero taken from it means something.
howTheSourceWasRendered.andItAlsoAnswersTheQuestion: The same control run showed 6,114 dark pixels LOST when annotations are drawn. That is the /AP /N opaque white fill covering page-content ink the form itself prints. It is the direct measurement that the stripped fills on this family masked PRINTED ART and not blank paper.
howTheSourceWasRendered.controlCopyBuiltBy: pdf-lib, page /Annots deleted and catalog /AcroForm dropped; used only as a control and never as a comparison baseline.

howTheStrippedFillsWereDecided.theQuestion: Restoring a fill that covered blank paper moves bytes for nothing; leaving one that masked printed art ships a doubled frame. The two lanes that reached opposite conclusions on this class today (Colorado, Nebraska) were both right, so the answer had to be measured on these pages.
howTheStrippedFillsWereDecided.theTest: At 600 dpi, inside each widget's own /Rect, count dark pixels three ways: the source with annotations OFF (page art alone), the source with annotations ON (what a viewer shows), and the delivered fixture.
howTheStrippedFillsWereDecided.resultOnThisCohort: COLORADO SHAPE, not Nebraska. On the order page 1 check boxes: page art alone 3,057 dark pixels per control; source as a viewer renders it 4,811; delivered 7,868 = 4,811 + 3,057 exactly. Both drawings are present at once in the delivered page. The form prints a heavy bracketed box, the /AP covers it with `1 g 0 0 18 18 re f` and strokes its own thin 17x17 square in its place, and stripping the fill revealed the bracket while still stamping the square.
howTheStrippedFillsWereDecided.crop: Rendered and read as an image: source page art alone is a thick bracketed box; the source as a viewer sees it is one clean thin square; the delivered page before repair carries BOTH, superimposed.
howTheStrippedFillsWereDecided.soTheRemedy: RESTORE the fill. Removing this ink would have deleted the Arkansas Crime Information Center's own check-box stroke from a petition and a proposed order.

aRTIFACTSObligationIsNotTheBorderFinding.whatTheObligationSays: generate-route-artifact-acceptance.mjs defines it as 'the route artifact's canonical and boundary bytes hash to what reports/rendered-artifacts.json names'.
aRTIFACTSObligationIsNotTheBorderFinding.measuredAtTheBaseBeforeAnyEdit: Every digest, byteLength and pageCount reports/rendered-artifacts.json named for BOTH families at base 8614b3e86 was recomputed with sha256sum, stat and pdfinfo and matched the bytes exactly. No hardcoded count, no stale digest and no unparsed pageCount was found in either delivered record.
aRTIFACTSObligationIsNotTheBorderFinding.whatWasActuallyMissing: ar-cs-possession-seal-set's record carried neither output-byte glyph reading and no pageCount at all; ar-nonconviction-seal-set's carried pageCount but neither glyph reading. Both now emit addedGlyphsReadFromOutputBytes, nonWhitespaceGlyphsOutsideMeasuredWriteBoxes, flattenedWidgetAppearancesReadFromOutputBytes and pageCount, every one read out of the produced PDF after it is written.
aRTIFACTSObligationIsNotTheBorderFinding.andTheByteFinding: vf90's row names ARTIFACTS for a different reason: the delivered artifacts carried flattened widget appearances matching no pinned-source /AP /N stream byte for byte. That is repaired too, and on its own terms -- see byteAccountingReproducedIndependently.

sharedModuleChanges: none modified. scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-active-content.mjs and rcap-official-form-finalize.mjs were read and NOT changed: the opt-in this repair needs (preserveUnwrittenSelectionBackgrounds) already exists there and defaults to false, so it is passed at each family's own builder. One NEW file was added, scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-output-glyph-reading.mjs, which is imported by these two builders and by nothing else; adding it cannot move any other family's bytes.
centralArtifactsEdited: none. MASTER_QUEUE.json, RASTER_QUEUE.json, claim-ledger.json, BORDER_COHORT_REMEDIATION.json and REPAIR_SUPPLY_QUEUE.json were read and not written. account-stroke-only-against-pinned-sources.mjs was NOT run, because it rewrites the shared ledger as a side effect.
verdictSet: none. This lane repairs and measures; it issues no PASS, sets no verdict and opens no route. A repair author does not verify their own candidate.

whatWasWrong.class: ink this packet UNCOVERED -- the court's own opaque white mask stripped out of every unwritten check-box appearance, revealing a printed box that the appearance was drawn to replace
whatWasWrong.widgets: 36 flattened stroke-only appearances across the four fixtures: 8 per petition fixture (field Check Box4 and its siblings on petition pages 1 and 2) and 10 per order fixture (field Check Box1 and its siblings on order pages 1 and 2).
whatWasWrong.cause:
Each of those widgets ships an /AP /N of `1 g
0 0 18 18 re
f
0.5 0.5 17 17 re
s` -- an opaque white fill the size of the widget's own BBox, then a thin 17x17 stroked square. stripOpaqueBackgroundPaint in scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-active-content.mjs removes a leading fill at grey >= 0.9 covering the widget, which is correct where the fill covers blank paper. Here the ACIC page content prints a heavy bracketed check box at each of those rectangles, the /AP covers it and strokes a cleaner one in its place, and with the fill gone the participant was handed the printed bracket AND the stamped square at every one of the 36 controls.
whatWasWrong.readOnThePage: 600 dpi, inside the widget /Rect on the order page 1: page art alone 3,057 dark pixels; source as a viewer renders it 4,811; delivered before this repair 7,868 = 4,811 + 3,057. After this repair the delivered page is pixel-identical to the source render inside those rects.
whatWasWrong.remedy: RESTORE -- preserveUnwrittenSelectionBackgrounds passed at this builder's own finalizeOfficialForm call. It keeps the source's authored blank-state paint on a selection this run did not write. /MK /BG is still removed, so no background the form did not itself author is requested, no mark is added and no box is ticked.
whatWasWrong.whyNotRemoval: BORDER_COHORT_REMEDIATION already records this family as EVERY_STROKE_IS_THE_FORMS_OWN_SOME_WITH_ITS_BACKGROUND_FILL_STRIPPED, whose remedy RESTORES. That label was reproduced here rather than trusted, and the pixels agree with it.

The delivered stroke-only streams reduce to 4 distinct streams on the petition and 1 on the order, all of them source /AP /N streams; none carries a show-text operator and none is a mark.

rows.blastRadius: scripts/build-census-v1-ar-cs-possession-seal-set.mjs declares this family alone. MASTER_QUEUE records exclusiveScript true and importedBy [] for it, and nothing in scripts/ or src/ imports it. The behavioural change is one option that defaults to false in the shared module, passed at this family's own call site, so no other family's next rebuild moves a byte because this family passes it. The new glyph-reading module is imported by these two builders and nothing else. Baseline reproducibility was established first: the UNCHANGED builder was run at base and reproduced all four committed fixtures byte for byte (git reported no diff), so every byte that moved afterwards is attributable to this repair.
